headline: How the Famous Nike Logo Was Created for $35

sentences.text: In 1971, Carolyn Davidson created a new shoe mark.
A business owner named Phil Knight needed a design.
The young student received $35 for her creative work.
Knight said he did not love the design at first.
Years later, the company gave her a gold ring.

grammar.title: Past Simple Negation
grammar.note: We use 'did not' followed by the base form of the verb to form past simple negatives. It shows an action that did not take place in the past. This structure remains the same regardless of the subject.

grammar.title: Ditransitive Verbs
grammar.note: Ditransitive verbs like 'give' can take two objects. In this sentence, 'her' is the indirect object receiving the item, and 'a gold ring' is the direct object being given.

sentences.text: In 1971, Carolyn Davidson was a student at Portland State University.
Phil Knight asked her to create a design showing fluid motion.
She worked for 17.5 hours, so Knight paid her $35 total.
Knight did not love the design, but he accepted the symbol.
The brand became famous, and Knight gave her stock in 1983.
Her simple creation will always stay famous around the whole world.

grammar.title: Verb + Object + To-Infinitive
grammar.note: The verb 'ask' follows the pattern of verb + object + to-infinitive. It expresses requesting someone to perform a specific action.

grammar.title: Linking Verbs with Adjectives
grammar.note: Linking verbs like 'become' connect the subject to an adjective complement that describes its condition. Here, 'famous' describes the subject 'The brand'.

sentences.text: In 1971, Carolyn Davidson was a university student who needed extra money for art class.
Phil Knight, who co-founded Blue Ribbon Sports, hired her for two dollars per hour.
He asked her to create a logo, which is a graphic symbol for brands.
Davidson designed the famous Swoosh, but Knight initially said he did not love it.
The company paid her $35 for 17.5 hours of work on the shoe design.
Since then, Nike has become huge and has given Davidson stock and a gold ring.

grammar.focus: who needed extra money for art class
grammar.title: Defining Relative Clauses
grammar.note: The relative pronoun 'who' introduces essential details about 'a university student'. Within its relative clause, 'who' acts directly as the subject.

grammar.title: Present Perfect Tense
grammar.note: The present perfect 'has become' connects a past event to the current situation. It emphasizes that the state achieved in the past remains true in the present.

sentences.text: In 1971, graphic design student Carolyn Davidson was hired by Blue Ribbon Sports co-founder Phil Knight.
Knight needed a new trademark, an official graphic symbol, for his upcoming athletic shoe line.
He asked Davidson to create a visual mark that conveyed dynamic motion and speed.
Davidson submitted several options, including the shape inspired by wings that was selected for production.
Upon choosing the design, Knight reportedly stated that he did not love it at first.
The company paid her an invoice of $35, which represented 17.5 hours of freelance work.
In 1983, Nike expressed gratitude by presenting Davidson stock shares and a diamond-embedded gold ring.

grammar.title: Passive Voice Construction
grammar.note: The passive voice places focus on the person receiving the action ('Carolyn Davidson'). It is formed using a past tense form of 'be' combined with the past participle 'hired'.

grammar.title: Preposition + Gerund
grammar.note: When a verb follows a preposition like 'by', it takes the -ing gerund form. This structure expresses the method used to accomplish an action.

sentences.text: In 1971, Portland State University graphic design student Carolyn Davidson accepted freelance work for Blue Ribbon Sports to fund art classes.
Co-founder Phil Knight, seeking a dynamic stripe logo to convey motion, offered her an hourly rate of two dollars.
Davidson spent 17.5 hours developing multiple concepts before presenting the iconic, wing-inspired curve that became known as the Swoosh.
Though Knight famously remarked that he did not love the design initially, tight production deadlines forced an immediate choice.
Davidson billed the company just $35 for her effort, a modest fee for creating a globally famous trademark.
The company officially adopted the name Nike in 1971 and introduced the emblem on athletic footwear the following year.
As the brand expanded into a global empire, Knight ensured that her early contribution was properly recognized.
In 1983, Knight presented Davidson with a diamond-set gold ring alongside 500 shares of company stock to show gratitude.

grammar.title: Participle Phrases as Modifiers
grammar.note: The present participle phrase 'seeking...' modifies the subject 'Co-founder Phil Knight'. It delivers background context concise and smoothly without needing a full clause.

grammar.title: Adverbial Clauses of Time
grammar.note: The subordinating conjunction 'As' introduces an adverbial clause showing time or concurrent progress. It sets the background frame for the main clause that follows.
